title: fix(active-memory): detect French recall intent in escalate mode
body:
Closes #171369

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Active Memory skips deep recall in its default escalate mode when users ask about earlier conversations in French.

## User Impact

French questions such as "Tu te souviens de ce qu'on a décidé pour le serveur ?" or "Qu'est-ce qu'on a dit pour Kyoto ?" now trigger recall when the lane-1 lookup has no strong hit. Unaccented spellings and curly apostrophes (common from mobile keyboards) are supported. Future reminders (with a future cue such as *demain* or *ce soir*) and everyday statements stay quiet; an ambiguous "Tu te souviens de/d' + X ?" goes to the recall model. Other languages and configuration defaults are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a French entry to the existing localized `{ intent, future, retrospective }` structure. Intent requires either recall-question phrasing (*tu te souviens*, *rappelle-moi ce que…*) or completed-discussion context (*on en a parlé*, *je t'ai dit*, *qu'est-ce qu'on a décidé*, a past-time marker near a discussion verb). Bare passé composé such as "On a décidé d'aller au cinéma ce soir." does not match: French *on* usually narrates the user's own life, not the conversation with the assistant. *Rappelle-moi de…* (remind me to) is a reminder and stays quiet.

## Evidence

**Review findings addressed** (`2117351`, supersedes the infinitive rule from `6c7877f`):
- The `-er`/`-ir` lookahead after "tu te souviens de/d'" is removed: it rejected proper names ("Tu te souviens de Roger ?") as remember-to verbs, and spelling can't separate the two. "Tu te souviens d'envoyer le rapport ?" (with or without "aujourd'hui") and "Vous vous rappelez de faire les courses ?" now **start recall**; the same questions with a future cue ("… demain ?") stay quiet through the French `future` guard.
- New positives: "Tu te souviens de Roger ?", "Te souviens-tu de Xavier ?", "Vous vous rappelez de Gauthier ?", "Tu te souviens d'Olivier ?", "Tu te souviens d'envoyer le rapport ?".

**Earlier review findings** (`6c7877f`):
- Discussion verbs and time markers carry letter/number boundaries in every alternative, so "crédit", "audit" and "cahier" no longer match `dit` / `hier`.

**Unit tests on `2117351`:** CI's node test jobs pass. Locally, all 160 `hasRecallIntent` table cases were checked against `escalation.ts` with Node 26 type stripping (not the Vitest runner): 160/160 on `2117351`; on `6c7877f` the five new positives fail.

**Unit tests on `6c7877f`:** focused `extensions/active-memory/escalation.test.ts` with the repo's pinned Vitest 5.0.1 on Node 24.21: **160 passed**. On `main` (`6e63f060fa7`), the French positive cases fail; the 115 existing cases across all languages are unchanged. New negatives covered "Tu te souviens d'envoyer le rapport ?", "… aujourd'hui ?" and "Vous vous rappelez de faire les courses ?" (moved to positives in `2117351`), "Hier j'ai payé à crédit.", "Hier on a fait un audit." and "J'ai dit que mon cahier était plein."; new positives cover "Tu te souviens d'avoir parlé de Kyoto ?", "… de notre voyage …" and "… de Pierre ?". `oxfmt --check` clean; `oxlint` with the repo's `.oxlintrc.json` (UI-only `solid-lint` plugin omitted): 0 findings.

**Live Gateway, Telegram DM** (OpenClaw 2026.10.3, Ubuntu 24.04, Active Memory `mode: "escalate"`, recall model Haiku, memory-core with local embeddings and a memory file from a real conversation two days earlier). This PR's French entry as of `6c7877f` was applied to the installed escalation chunk, with debug logging; both reverted afterwards. Each message was sent after `/new`:

| Message | Escalation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| "Tu te souviens de ce que tu m'avais conseillé pour passer le serveur à 4 Go ?" | recall | recall sub-agent called `memory_search`; top hit = the seeded memory file (score 0.68); `done status=ok`, 795-char summary injected into the reply prompt |
| "Tu te souviens d'envoyer le rapport ?" | skipped *(`6c7877f` only)* | `recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent`, no recall-model request. **Superseded:** with `2117351` this message starts recall (see above) |
| "Hier j'ai payé à crédit." | skipped | `recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent`, no recall-model request |

<details>
<summary>Redacted gateway log lines</summary>

```
21:50:07.974 INFO  active-memory: agent=<agent> session=agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<redacted> activeModel=claude-haiku-5-5 start timeoutMs=15000 queryChars=77
21:50:15.101 DEBUG embedded run tool end: runId=active-memory-<id> tool=memory_search
21:50:16.061 DEBUG embedded run tool end: runId=active-memory-<id> tool=memory_search
21:50:23.048 INFO  active-memory: agent=<agent> session=agent:<agent>:telegram:direct:<redacted> activeModel=claude-haiku-5-5 done status=ok elapsedMs=15074 summaryChars=795
21:46:00.842 DEBUG active-memory: recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent    # "Tu te souviens d'envoyer le rapport ?" (6c7877f; recalls on 2117351)
21:46:28.240 DEBUG active-memory: recall skipped reason=no-recall-intent    # "Hier j'ai payé à crédit."
```
</details>

An earlier run of the first message with this install's `promptStyle: "preference-only"` also escalated and retrieved the same memory, but the recall model answered NONE (the preference-only prompt filters out conversation recall). The run above uses `promptStyle: "balanced"`; the escalation decision is identical in both.
